factual_errors.text: A hot wire can burn, so keep the current small. One cell's low potential difference gives no risk of an electric shock. That keeps it at a constant temperature, which means its temperature stays the same.
factual_errors.correction: Because of the sentence order, 'That' now refers to the low potential difference removing the shock risk, so the text says the low p.d. is what keeps the wire at constant temperature. It is keeping the current small and switching off between readings that stops the wire heating and keeps it at constant temperature. The safety sentences should not sit between the method and its reason.
